title: Bento grid: token ownership and variant contracts for controls
creator: Maya Gonzalez
description:
Problem statement: Over the last two quarters we've accumulated inconsistent token ownership for spacing/size primitives used across button/table/chart control variants. Multiple instances of the same primitive exist with divergent autolayout constraints and undocumented intent (density vs. touch targets). This causes regressions during library publishes and creates friction for engineers consuming variants.

Goal: Establish clear ownership and immutable contracts for the core 'bento' layout primitives (row-gap, column-gap, control-padding, control-height), normalize auto-layout constraints across control variants, and add a publish-time checklist + lightweight rollback mechanism so accidental token edits can be reverted before they impact product builds.

Scope:
- Audit and canonicalize token names and aliases for spacing and control sizing used by buttons, input rows, table row controls, and small chart controls.
- Standardize auto-layout constraints for 'compact' and 'comfortable' density variants; create constraints templates in Figma.
- Add token provenance (owner, last-modified, rationale) as a component-level annotation where practical.
- Create a pre-publish CI checklist and a short 'rollback recipe' documented in Confluence.
- Implement an acceptance checklist for design reviewers and QA prior to Figma library publish.

Out of scope: Deep refactor of chart atoms, replacing tokens across entire platform (this work focuses on controls and immediate dependent primitives).
acceptance_criteria: All bento tokens have canonical names and alias map documented in Confluence with owner assigned
Compact and comfortable density variants share the same auto-layout templates and pass visual diff checks on 3 representative pages
Figma publish pipeline includes a checklist step and at least one manual rollback test documented
Design reviewers sign off on updated variant contracts and token ownership doc
No production stylesheets in staging reference deprecated token names after a sync pass with engineering
